pages.text: Apotheosis replaces vanilla enchanting. The enchanting table is still there, but the bookshelves around it decide how it behaves.$(br2)$(bold)Main difference:$() you earn powerful enchants at the table. Chests still hold enchanted books, but treasure enchants such as Mending are rare in them, and no villager sells a book.

$(bold)Bookshelf Tiers$()$(br2)Each kind of bookshelf opens a different enchantment pool:$(li)Vanilla bookshelves: basic enchants, lower max level$(li)Apotheosis shelves: higher max level, wider pool$(li)Dimensional shelves (crafted from dimensional materials): rare enchants, max-level options$(br2)A high-tier enchanting setup is a real investment and a major Tier 2 to 3 project.

$(bold)Gem Sockets & Enchanting$()$(br2)Apotheosis affixes add gem sockets to items. Gems and enchants are separate systems, and both apply at the same time: a Legendary sword can have maximum enchants and 4 perfect gems.

$(bold)Villagers Sell No Books$()$(br2)No villager sells an enchanted book, and no villager or wandering trader sells diamonds or diamond gear. Emeralds buy convenience: food, building blocks, light, iron tools and armor, and XP bottles from a journeyman cleric on.$(br2)For enchants, use the table or the $(l:icraft:loot/relic_economy)Relic Broker$(/l). A villager keeps the trades it already offers.

$(bold)Anvil cap removed:$() Apotheosis removes the vanilla 'Too Expensive' cap, so you can combine and repair items as many times as you need. XP costs rise but never become impossible.$(br2)$(bold)Next: upgrade your bookshelves.$()
